stories.title: 'The crowd shouted that we'd stolen someone's genitals' - deadly rumours spread on social media
stories.summary: More than 80 people were killed between October 2025 and July this year following false accusations about what is termed "genital theft", the BBC Global Disinformation Unit has found after gathering data from police forces across six African countries. The killings are linked to rumours that a simple tap on the shoulder can cause a man's genitals to shrink or disappear. They are being fuelled by widespread misinformation on social media. "They were shouting that we had stolen someone's genitals and we didn't have any way to escape because there was a huge crowd," Tanzanian mechanic. Boniface Mgala told the BBC about his ordeal in April when he was badly beaten by those convinced he was a genital thief. His experience was similar to those in videos seen by the BBC: men claim that their genital organs - penis and testicles - have vanished or shrivelled after coming into contact with strangers and a mob then demands that alleged perpetrators return what they have supposedly stolen. Such claims are rooted in longstanding fears and superstitions - and are not new on the continent, particularly in communities where belief in witchcraft remains widespread. Social media has amplified these fears. The recent wave of rumours appears to have started last year in the Democratic Republic of Congo, where similar claims had surfaced in 2008. They progressively spread across the region to Burundi, Zambia and Tanzania as well as Mozambique, Angola, Malawi and Kenya. In Zambia, the hearsay about disappearing genitals first gained traction in March when a woman was lynched, going on to spread panic across the border in Tanzania. At his home in Mpemba near Tunduma, a busy trading town in Tanzania by the border with Zambia, Mgala traces his fingers along the sickle-shaped scar that runs down the right side of his head as he reflects on his traumatic experience.

stories.title: Coalition plan to cut tobacco excise by 80% ‘will kill people’ Labor says amid public health alarm
stories.summary: Angus Taylor and Matt Canavan claim drastic cut to price of cigarettes and moves to legalise vapes will combat illicit tobacco trade Leading public health experts, the Australian Medical Association and Labor have rejected Angus Taylor’s plan to cut tobacco excise by 80%, labelling the move to curb soaring illegal cigarette sales as a backward step on tobacco control. Taylor and Nationals leader Matt Canavan on Thursday announced plans for an 80% cut to excise, as well as moves to legalise and regulate vapes and nicotine pouches. The announcement comes weeks after One Nation leader Pauline Hanson proposed a 75% cut. Continue reading...

stories.title: Powerful storm hits Canada’s Toronto, cutting power to tens of thousands
stories.summary: Thunderstorm also causes severe flooding and forces flight cancellations at Pearson airport. A powerful thunderstorm has hit Canada’s largest city, Toronto, damaging buildings, closing roads and cutting power to tens of thousands of residents. The storm on Wednesday brought torrential rain, strong winds, and large hail, prompting tornado watches and warnings in some areas. At least 45,000 customers were without electricity as of 8pm on Wednesday (00:00 GMT on Thursday), according to electricity provider Toronto Hydro. The storm brought down trees and caused flooding, prompting road closures in the city, including on the Don Valley Parkway, the CBC reported. The Michael Garron Hospital, located in Toronto’s East York community, said its emergency department has been affected by flooding. Images published by the CBC showed cars nearly submerged in the city of Vaughan, north of Toronto. Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow said in a post on X that the city’s emergency operations centre has been activated since Wednesday morning. “City crews are already out responding to downed power wires, fallen trees, flooding and more,” she said. The Toronto Transit Commission, which operates subways and buses, “is working to restore service where it has been affected by flooding and debris spread by high winds”, she added. Dozens of flights set to depart Toronto Pearson International airport on Wednesday evening were either delayed or cancelled. Canada’s weather agency, Environment and Climate Change Canada, lifted an orange warning for severe thunderstorms in the Greater Toronto Area.
